summary: The recall against you: {organizer} has filed to recall you, and {donor} has just promised to pay for the signatures.
realLife: One life: A recall drive against the California governor stalled until a congressman gave $2 million in 2003. The low turnout of the 2002 race had lowered the signatures needed. He signed bills his base wanted and apologized for being slow on the energy crisis, and was recalled. Another: Recall organizers gathered about 900,000 signatures, and he raised over $30 million. In 2012 he became the first governor to survive a recall; recalls of senators the same day briefly flipped the state Senate.
gates: You hold an office that the place's law lets voters recall.
A recall petition against you is on record.
weights: How many signatures are needed, from the last race's turnout.
choices: sign laws your own voters want
raise far more money than they can

branches.when: turnout was low in your last race
branches.then: The low turnout in your own last race made the signature count small (C32).
A newcomer wins the replacement vote. You concede and offer help with the handover (C43).
You are the first in your office to survive one, and recalls of members on the same day change who controls {the body}.

branches.when: you sign bills to win back your base
branches.then: Your base stays cool, and the polls do not move.
